info.name: Uber Ride-Hailing API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Go ride-hailing microservices system.

**Setup:**
1. Import this collection into Postman
2. Base URL is pre-set to `http://localhost:8000`
3. Run requests in order — tokens and IDs are auto-captured via test scripts

**Architecture:** 6 microservices + API Gateway (NGINX :8000)
**Flow:** Register → Login → Driver Go Online → Set Location → Request Trip → (3s wait) → Verify Assignment → Start Trip → End Trip → Rate → View Payment/Notifications

request.description: Health check served directly by NGINX — no backend involved. Confirms the gateway itself is running.
Health check for user-service (routed via NGINX gateway).

Create a new rider account. Returns JWT tokens and user profile.

**Validation rules:**
- name: 2–200 chars
- email: valid format
- phone: E.164 format (e.g. +919999999999)
- password: minimum 6 chars
2FA Step 1 — validates password and sends a 6-digit OTP to the rider's email. Returns 202 with no token. Check email for OTP, then run Verify Rider Login.

item.name: Verify Rider Login (Step 2 — exchange OTP for JWT)

request.description: 2FA Step 2 — verifies the OTP from email and issues access + refresh tokens. Set the `riderOTP` collection variable to the code from your inbox before running.

Get a new access token using the rider's refresh token.

**Note:** Run Login Rider first to populate `rider_refresh_token`.
Fetch rider profile by ID. Must be authenticated as the same rider (IDOR protection).
Create a new driver account with vehicle details.
2FA Step 1 — validates password and sends a 6-digit OTP to the driver's email. Returns 202 with no token. Check email for OTP, then run Verify Driver Login.

item.name: Verify Driver Login (Step 2 — exchange OTP for JWT)

request.description: 2FA Step 2 — verifies the OTP from email and issues access + refresh tokens. Set the `driverOTP` collection variable to the code from your inbox before running.

Get a new access token using the driver's refresh token.

**Note:** Run Login Driver first to populate `driver_refresh_token`.
Fetch driver profile by ID. Must be authenticated as the same driver (IDOR protection).

Update driver's availability status. Must be done before setting location.

**Valid values:** `available`, `busy`, `offline`

Update driver's GPS position in Redis GEO set. Must be done before a rider can request a trip.

**Coordinates:** Bangalore city center (12.9716, 77.5946)

Find available drivers within radius km using Redis GEO search.

**Requires driver JWT** (driver role only).

Get fare estimate before requesting a trip. No DB or Kafka involved.

**Fare formula:** ₹50 (base) + ₹12 × distance_km

Request a new ride. Publishes `ride.requested` to Kafka → Matching service finds driver → publishes `driver.assigned`.

**Wait ~3 seconds, then call Get Trip Details to verify DRIVER_ASSIGNED status.**

Prerequisites: Driver must be `available` and have set their location.

Fetch full trip details by ID. Call this ~3 seconds after Request Trip to verify driver was assigned.

**Trip statuses:** REQUESTED → DRIVER_ASSIGNED → STARTED → COMPLETED / CANCELLED
Manually assign a driver to a REQUESTED trip (bypasses automatic Kafka matching).

Move trip to STARTED state. Only the assigned driver can call this.

Prerequisite: Trip must be in DRIVER_ASSIGNED status.

Complete a trip. Fare is auto-calculated using Haversine formula from pickup/drop coordinates.

Publishes `trip.completed` → Payment service auto-creates payment.

Prerequisite: Trip must be in STARTED status.
Cancel a trip (REQUESTED or DRIVER_ASSIGNED). Restores driver to Redis GEO pool and publishes `trip.cancelled` event.

Submit a rating (1–5) for a completed trip. Each rater can only rate once per trip (UNIQUE constraint).

Publishes `rating.submitted` → Driver/User service updates average rating.
Get user's trip history (works for both riders and drivers).

Fetch payment details for a completed trip. Payment is auto-created ~1 second after trip ends.

Wait 2 seconds after End Trip before calling this.
Get user's payment history (rider or driver).

Get user's notifications. Test script auto-captures the first notification ID.

**Notification types:** ride_requested, driver_assigned, trip_completed, trip_cancelled, rating_submitted, payment_completed

Mark a notification as read.

**Prerequisite:** Run Get Notifications first to auto-populate `notification_id`.

**WebSocket endpoint** — real-time trip location tracking.

Cannot be tested via HTTP in Postman. Use a WebSocket client:

```bash
# wscat
wscat -c ws://localhost:8000/ws/trips/$TRIP_ID

# websocat
websocat ws://localhost:8000/ws/trips/$TRIP_ID
```

**Server pushes JSON on driver location update:**
```json
{
  "trip_id": "...",
  "lat": 12.9720,
  "lng": 77.5950,
  "ts": 1741000000
}
```
